title: totec448-spec/chat-on-steroids
abstract: All downloads Independent beta. Use at your own risk and within your provider's rules. Read the usage notice before connecting. Get started · Watch the demo · What’s new Code. Delegate. Keep going. Work on the real project. Let ChatGPT read and edit files, run tests, keep terminals open and use your desktop. Follow the actual tool results as they arrive. Give it a team. Split independent jobs across workers, then bring their results back. Workers keep their context, so the next task can pick up where they left off. Stay in control of long tasks. Send a correction while work runs. Goal follows unfinished work; Loop keeps working within your brief. Compact & Resume carries the session and worker history into a fresh chat. Uses your ChatGPT conversation rather than invoking Codex directly. ChatGPT Work and Codex share usage limits. Your account’s model availability, usage and context limits still apply. OpenAI usage details → What you get When it needs a human, it says so Some steps only you can do: a sign-in, a USB key, a command it must not run. ChatGPT hands you a step for you , with the exact command, the folder and what it expects to see. You run it yourself and mark it done ; the app never runs it. Know what your chats are doing, away from your desk Get a message when a chat finishes, needs you or fails, through the free ntfy app or a Telegram bot of your own . With Telegram you can also ask /status , stop or pause a chat, and deny an approval from your phone. Nothing can be allowed remotely. When a chat is stuck, one row tells you why Since when, how often the app tried, and every step it took. It turns amber once the app has stopped trying, so you know when it needs you. Give a project more context, not more access Add related folders to a project so ChatGPT knows about them. They never become the working folder and never widen what it may touch. Link your own Telegram bot in a minute Create a bot with @BotFather, paste its token, and send the shown code to it. Notifications then also arrive in Telegram. ntfy keeps working until you turn its switch off in the phone notification settings, and with "Include chat names and answers" on, either one can carry chat names and answers. Keep chats in projects Move a chat into a project from its menu or by dragging it, and undo it right away. Chats are grouped by date, and a project's folder is where its chats work. Pick the model and effort per chat , with the same controls ChatGPT offers. Folders you control. Choose exactly which folders ChatGPT may touch, and what it may do there. Limit how many chats work at once , so a busy day does not hit your usage in one burst. Command output in a dock. Watch what a running command prints, read-only, and stop it with one click. Skills, plugins and pets , 13 languages, light and dark. Responsible use and provider rules Chat On Steroids is an independent, open-source workspace for coding and other authorized tasks with your own files and tools. It is intended to support productive work within the rules of the services you use. It is not intended to bypass usage limits, account restrictions or safety controls. Use CoS in accordance with OpenAI's applicable Terms of Use ( Europe Terms for the EEA, Switzerland and UK), Usage Policies and Service Terms , plus your workspace's rules and any connected service's terms. Respect limits and access decisions. Workers, Goal/Loop, Compact & Resume and finish checkpoints organize work; they do not grant extra quota or model access and must not be used to evade rate limits, usage caps or account restrictions. Do not switch accounts, chats, plugins or tunnels to evade a restriction. Respect safety decisions. Do not use local tools, browser control, plugins or another worker to carry out an action that the provider blocked for safety. A local permission or an enabled MCP plugin is not permission to override a provider refusal. Understand the integration. CoS connects local tools through MCP. Its browser extension also observes and automates the ChatGPT browser UI and records conversation content locally. This browser integration is not a public ChatGPT automation API. MCP availability does not establish permission for every form of browser automation or recording; OpenAI's terms also restrict automated or programmatic extraction of data or output. Use at your own risk. Review the rules for your account and intended workflow before connecting, supervise automation and review tool actions and outputs. CoS cannot guarantee policy compliance, continued service access or protection from account warnings, restrictions or suspension. If a workflow is restricted or receives a policy warning, stop that workflow and seek clarification through the provider's support or appeal process. This notice states the project's intended use; it does not certify compliance or change provider rules. CoS is not affiliated with, endorsed by or approved by OpenAI. The software is provided as-is under the MIT license ; applicable statutory rights remain unaffected. See Security for local permissions and risks. Get started Install CoS and open Settings → Setup . It walks you through seven short steps, with pictures of what to click. Connect your browser (step 1): load the browser extension in Chrome, Edge or Brave. Setup shows your browser's own extensions page in your language: turn on Developer mode , click Load unpacked and choose the folder that Open extension folder shows. Pairing is automatic. Share a folder and choose access (steps 2–3): the folder ChatGPT may work in, and what it may do there. Connect Core (steps 4–7): create a tunnel and a restricted API key at OpenAI, press Connect , then add the app in ChatGPT under Plugins → Add → Add custom MCP server . Tunnel setup → Choose a model, write your task and send. Requirements & installation notes Windows 10/11, macOS 13 Ventura or newer , or a current desktop Linux. Chrome 125+, current Edge or Brave, plus a ChatGPT account/workspace that can create custom MCP apps (availability depends on your plan and workspace policy). Check account availability . Unsigned beta: Windows is not publisher-signed; macOS is unsigned and unnotarized. Verify the package against the release checksums. Because of that, macOS asks once after each update for your login password so the new version can open its saved keys ("chat-on-steroids Safe Storage"); choose Always Allow . Until you answer, chats and the browser connection wait, and the app says so. Linux: a Secret Service keyring is required. Prefer the DEB; when unprivileged user namespaces are disabled, the AppImage launcher can fall back to --no-sandbox . Permissions: choose your approved folders and review capabilities before connecting. Fresh installs enable Core capabilities and two workers; Windows also enables Desktop permissions. Shell commands run with your normal user privileges. Languages: English, German, Spanish, French, Korean, Portuguese (Brazil and Portugal), Russian, Turkish, Vietnamese, Japanese, and Simplified and Traditional Chinese. Choose one in Appearance → Language . After updating: the browser extension updates itself once no chat is busy. If CoS asks you to refresh its apps in ChatGPT, do so; Automatic plugin refresh in Settings can do it for you. Folder and capability settings Setup & help · Docs · Plugins · Contribute · Security · MIT license Built with our community contributors . Thank you to the people behind the code, designs, bug reports and testing. Not affiliated with or endorsed by OpenAI. ChatGPT and Codex are OpenAI trademarks.

title: moeru-ai/airi
abstract:
Project AIRI Re-creating Neuro-sama, a soul container of AI waifu / virtual characters to bring them into our world. [ Join Discord Server ] [ Try it ] [ 簡體中文 ] [ 日本語 ] [ Русский ] [ Tiếng Việt ] [ Français ] [ 한국어 ] Heavily inspired by Neuro-sama Tip On Windows, you can also install AIRI with winget : winget install MoeruAI.AIRI Or install AIRI with Scoop : scoop bucket add airi https: // github.com / moeru - ai / airi
scoop install airi / airi On macOS, you can install AIRI with Homebrew Cask without adding a custom tap: brew install --cask airi Warning Attention: We do not have any officially minted cryptocurrency or token associated with this project. Please check the information and proceed with caution. Note We've got a whole dedicated organization @proj-airi for all the sub-projects born from Project AIRI. Check it out! RAG, memory system, embedded database, icons, Live2D utilities, and more! Tip You can translate AIRI on Crowdin , or open a pull request that changes packages/i18n/src/locales/ . Both ways update the same translations. Do not submit a translation that is the same as the English text. Review rejects it. A string without a translation shows the English text. Have you dreamed about having a cyber living being (cyber waifu, digital pet) or digital companion that could play with and talk to you? With the power of modern large language models like ChatGPT and famous Claude , asking a virtual being to roleplay and chat with us is already easy enough for everyone. Platforms like Character.ai (a.k.a. c.ai) and JanitorAI as well as local playgrounds like SillyTavern are already good-enough solutions for a chat based or visual adventure game like experience. But, what about the abilities to play games? And see what you are coding at? Chatting while playing games, watching videos, and is capable of doing many other things. Perhaps you know Neuro-sama already. She is currently the best virtual streamer capable of playing games, chatting, and interacting with you and the participants. Some also call this kind of being "digital human." Sadly, as it's not open sourced, you cannot interact with her after her live streams go offline . Therefore, this project, AIRI, offers another possibility here: let you own your digital life, cyber living, easily, anywhere, anytime . Recent DevLogs & Stories DevLog @ 2026.03.23: Mobile performance and game engine exploration - March 23, 2026 DevLog @ 2026.03.14: VRM stage lifecycle, cache, and observability - March 14, 2026 DevLog @ 2026.02.16: Dome Keeper data collection and training pipeline - February 16, 2026 DevLog @ 2026.01.01: AIRI Pocket and FlowChat memory experiments - January 1, 2026 DevLog @ 2025.10.20: Electron migration, new models, and Moeru AI updates - October 20, 2025 DevLog @ 2025.08.26: Pure vision progress for airi-factorio - August 26, 2025 DevLog @ 2025.08.05: AIRI v0.7 release highlights - August 5, 2025 DevLog @ 2025.08.01: Streaming text animation and grapheme clusters - August 1, 2025 DevLog @ 2025.07.18: Rethinking airi-factorio with Factorio Learning Environment - July 18, 2025 DreamLog 0x1: The backstory of Project AIRI - June 16, 2025 More on the documentation site What's So Special About This Project? Unlike the other AI driven VTuber open source projects, アイリ was built with support of many Web technologies such as WebGPU , WebAudio , Web Workers , WebAssembly , WebSocket , etc. from the first day. Tip Worrying about the performance drop since we are using Web related technologies? Don't worry, while the Web browser version is meant to give an insight into how much we can push and do inside browsers and webviews, we will never fully rely on this. The desktop version of AIRI is capable of using native NVIDIA CUDA and Apple Metal by default (thanks to HuggingFace & the beloved candle project), without any complex dependency management. Considering the tradeoff, it is partially powered by Web technologies for graphics, layouts, animations, and the WIP plugin system for everyone to integrate things. This means that アイリ is capable of running on modern browsers and devices and even on mobile devices (already done with PWA support). This brings a lot of possibilities for us (the developers) to build and extend the power of アイリ VTuber to the next level, while still leaving the flexibility for users to enable features that require TCP connections or other non-Web technologies such as connecting to a Discord voice channel or playing Minecraft and Factorio with friends. Note We are still in the early stage of development where we are seeking out talented developers to join us and help us to make アイリ a reality. It's ok if you are not familiar with Vue.js, TypeScript, and devtools required for this project, you can join us as an artist, designer, or even help us to launch our first live stream. Even if you are a big fan of React, Svelte or even Solid, we welcome you. You can open a sub-directory to add features that you want to see in アイリ, or would like to experiment with. Fields (and related projects) that we are looking for: Live2D modeller VRM modeller VRChat avatar designer Computer Vision Reinforcement Learning Speech Recognition Speech Synthesis ONNX Runtime Transformers.js vLLM WebGPU Three.js WebXR ( checkout the another project we have under the @moeru-ai organization) If you are interested, why not introduce yourself here? Would like to join part of us to build AIRI? Current Progress & Roadmap Capable of Brain Play Minecraft Play Factorio (WIP, but PoC and demo available ) Play Kerbal Space Program (announcement TBD) Co-play Helldivers 2 (WIP) Chat in Telegram Chat in Discord Memory Pure in-browser database support (DuckDB WASM | pglite ) Memory Alaya (WIP) Pure in-browser local (WebGPU) inference Ears Audio input from browser Audio input from Discord Client side speech recognition Client side talking detection Mouth Multi-provider voice synthesis, including ElevenLabs , Microsoft/Azure Speech, OpenAI-compatible TTS, Alibaba Cloud Model Studio, and local Kokoro TTS Body VRM support Control VRM model VRM model animations Auto blink Auto look at Idle eye movement Live2D support Control Live2D model Live2D model animations Auto blink Auto look at Idle eye movement Development For detailed instructions to develop this project, follow CONTRIBUTING.md Note By default, pnpm dev will start the development server for the Stage Web (browser version). If you would
like to try developing the desktop version, please make sure you read CONTRIBUTING.md to setup the environment correctly. pnpm i
pnpm dev Stage Web (Browser Version at airi.moeru.ai ) pnpm dev Stage Tamagotchi (Desktop Version) pnpm dev:tamagotchi A Nix package for Tamagotchi is included. To run airi with Nix, first make sure to enable flakes, then run: nix run github:moeru-ai/airi NixOS Electron requires shared libraries that aren't in standard paths on NixOS. Use the FHS shell defined in flake.nix : nix develop . # fhs pnpm dev:tamagotchi Stage Pocket (Mobile Version) Start the development server for the capacitor: pnpm dev:pocket:ios --target " <DEVICE_ID_OR_SIMULATOR_NAME> " # Or CAPACITOR_DEVICE_ID_IOS= " <DEVICE_ID_OR_SIMULATOR_NAME> " pnpm dev:pocket:ios Quote the target: simulator names such as iPhone 16 Pro contain spaces. You can see the list of available devices and simulators by running pnpm -F @proj-airi/stage-pocket exec cap run ios --list . @capacitor/cli is declared in apps/stage-pocket , so cap does not resolve from the repository root. If you need to connect server channel on pocket in wireless mode, you need to start tamagotchi as root: sudo pnpm dev:tamagotchi Then enable secure websocket in tamagotchi settings/connections . Documentation Site The documentation site lives in moeru-ai/airi-docs . Publish Run bumpp to update the monorepo version: npx bumpp --no-commit --no-tag Support of LLM API Providers (powered by xsai ) AIHubMix (recommended) OpenRouter vLLM SGLang Ollama 302.

title: Narcooo/inkos
abstract:
Story Creation AI Agent 面向長短篇小說、劇本劇作、互動影遊、IP 內容與多語言翻譯的創作智慧體系統 English | 中文 | 日本語 InkOS 網頁版上線！ 立刻體驗 InkOS 是一個面向故事創作與多語言翻譯的 AI Agent 系統：長篇連載、獨立短篇、劇本劇作、同人番外、仿寫續寫、互動影遊、開放世界和長文翻譯，都可以從同一個工作臺開始。支援 Studio、TUI、CLI 互動形式，把創意、設定、角色、記憶、審稿、修訂、封面、互動狀態和跨語言交付交給智慧體統一管理。 🎉🎉 InkOS 入選首批 KIMI 開源合作夥伴 🎉🎉 感謝 Kimi 贊助本專案！Kimi K3 是 Moonshot AI 迄今能力最強的模型，也是全球首個開源 3T 級模型，擁有原生視覺能力與 100 萬 Token 上下文。搭配 InkOS，K3 可以參與長短篇小說、劇本、互動影遊與多語言內容的規劃、寫作、審稿和修訂；InkOS 則持續管理角色、設定、伏筆與故事狀態，讓長篇創作更連貫、更可控。 kkaiapi ｜一個 Key 調模型，一個 MCP 接資料與工具。 支援 Claude、GPT、Gemini、DeepSeek 等主流模型，按量付費、共用餘額，用於 InkOS 寫作、審稿與封面生成。 檢視模型與價格 → · InkOS 接入指南 → · MCP 接入 → 💡 寫小說，先給 Agent 接一層專業資料 —— 寫小說不只缺模型，更缺素材。推薦搭配 火花資料API（huohuaapi） ：按呼叫計費的小說 / 網文創作資料，讓 Agent 動筆前先查小說正文、章節結構、人物設定、文風和創作方法等帶來源素材，而不是只靠 Prompt 硬湊一份“劇情提綱”。 v2.0.0 - 統一 Pi Agent Harness 與專業創作核心 本分支為 2.0 開發版本，使用本地構建進行驗證。舊專案先執行 inkos work migrate --json 檢視升級清單，再執行 inkos work migrate --apply 匯入統一創作庫；原目錄與早期版本清單備份會保留，衝突不會覆蓋已有作品。 遷移會轉換 1.x 的書籍預設配置、規則和狀態快照，保留正文、原始目錄及未填寫的歷史資訊。舊寫作控制欄位保留在原件中，2.0 使用 Profile 的操作策略。缺少執行時狀態的專案以草稿進入創作庫，需完成狀態重建後再繼續生產。 本地開發與真實生產驗收統一使用 kkaiapi（ https://api.kkaiapi.com/v1 ）：文字按 DeepSeek V4 Flash / Pro 分工，封面使用 gpt-image-2 。在專案 llm.cover 中配置服務和模型，CLI 與 Studio 讀取同一配置，封面可複用 kkaiapi 服務金鑰。 已有短篇可以在作品對話中要求按審稿意見整篇修訂，或執行 inkos short revise <story-id> --instruction "修復審稿指出的時間線與證據鏈問題" 。系統會更新相關章節、大綱和銷售包，再次審稿，並保留原稿版本。 InkOS 2.0 把“Chat Agent 調工具”和“各類作品管線”收斂成一套圍繞 pi-agent 的生產 harness。模型負責理解、提議和呼叫能力；InkOS 負責確認、上下文、狀態、原子落盤和產物真實性。長篇、短篇、劇本、分鏡、互動影遊、Play 與翻譯繼續保留各自的專業方法，但共享同一套執行、檢索、觀測和恢復基礎設施。 模型配置 ：Studio 內建多服務配置、模型路由和封面服務配置；支援 kkaiapi / OpenRouter 等全球主流模型聚合入口，以及自定義 OpenAI Chat Completions、OpenAI Responses 和 Anthropic Messages 服務。 單一生產 Harness ：Studio Chat、TUI、 inkos interact 與生產 worker 共用 pi-agent 工具迴圈和結構化 action/result；既有 pipeline 降為可直接呼叫、可中斷、可觀測的確定效能力，不再維護平行的自然語言決策核心。 19 個內建專業 Skills ：長篇寫作 / 審稿、商業短篇、Play、劇本、分鏡、互動影遊、翻譯、拆稿、市場研究、匯入、封面與去 AI 味都擁有獨立 SKILL.md ；各作品型別複用 Skill 架構，不復用不適合自己的長篇提示詞。 統一本地檢索 ：故事記憶、材料庫和 Skill 參考資料共用 SQLite FTS5 / BM25 檢索投影；原始檔案仍是權威來源，索引可重建，檢索結果保留來源與位置。 書籍參考資料綁定 ：匯入材料可以顯式綁定到某本書並宣告用途，寫作時按當前任務檢索相關段落，而不是把所有檔案全文塞進上下文。 安全章節工作區 ：正文、狀態、伏筆和執行快照先在章節工作區內校驗，再原子提交；失敗不會出現“狀態已推進、正文未落盤”。Studio 可檢視改寫工作區和真實審稿問題。 跨作品生產一致性 ：Short、劇本、分鏡、互動影遊、Play 與翻譯接入統一 run snapshot、Skill 綁定、字數觀測、取消訊號和失敗恢復，同時保留各自的狀態模型與創作規則。 長任務與模型呼叫更穩 ：多章寫作按一個可恢復任務順序執行；首 Token / 流式空閒超時、過期狀態修復和原子檔案集降低被動卡住或半完成的機率。 TUI 對齊 Studio ：新增 /new 、 /short 、 /play 、 /cover 、 /write 明確入口，結構化 /confirm / /cancel ，會話級 /model 切換和明暗終端自適應配色；普通自由文本仍交給 Agent 理解。 模型與工作臺補齊 ：新增 LM Studio 本地服務，動態模型目錄和外部母本匯入可持久化；Studio 支援自定義封面 Base URL、寬屏章節預覽和安全章節重寫。 主要創作形態 長篇小說 — 從創作簡報建書，生成世界觀、角色、卷綱和章節意圖；寫作、審稿、修訂、狀態結算都是可獨立呼叫、可追溯的 Harness action。上下文按 protected / compressible 分層組織，避免長書越寫越亂。 劇情多線推演 — 在寫下一章前，基於當前正史生成 2-5 條彼此隔離的未來分支，並在 Studio Chat 中橫向比較章節節拍、人物決定、預計變化、風險和作者意圖匹配度。採用分支只會儲存 selected-branch-plan.md 候選計劃，不會修改正文、大綱或正史狀態；正史變化後舊推演會標記為過期。 InkOS Short — Studio Chat 和 CLI 可以直接產出獨立短篇：完整正文、大綱記錄、審稿記錄、簡介賣點、封面提示詞，並在配置封面服務後生成封面圖。 InkOS Play — 新增開放世界與分支互動。你可以用自然語言指定世界契約、時間推進方式、角色 agent、物品 / 證據 / 關係規則和視覺風格；系統維護世界狀態、可點選選擇、自由動作、HUD 和自動配圖。 Studio Chat — 普通聊天、建書、短篇、封面、互動世界都走同一套 action surface。重動作先確認，生成物可預覽，可通過聊天修改章節、封面提示詞、世界狀態和持久化文本產物。 Native English novel writing now supported！ Set --lang en to write in English. See English README for details. 歡迎交流 當前更新相對頻繁，後續會持續新增功能與最佳化寫作效果。
歡迎加群反饋問題、提出需求，也歡迎關注專案動態 — 我們的目標是做最強的基於小說的內容生態創作 AI Agent。 快速開始 安裝 需要 Node.js 22.16 或更高版本 。 npm i -g @actalk/inkos 通過 OpenClaw 使用 🦞 InkOS 已釋出為 OpenClaw Skill，可被任何相容 Agent（Claude Code、OpenClaw 等）直接呼叫： clawhub install inkos # 從 ClawHub 安裝 InkOS Skill 通過 npm 安裝或克隆本專案時， skills/SKILL.md 已包含在內，🦞 可直接讀取——無需額外從 ClawHub 安裝。 安裝後，Claw 應優先通過共享互動入口呼叫 InkOS： inkos interact --json --message " 繼續當前書，但把節奏再收緊一點 " 這條入口直接走和專案 TUI 相同的互動執行核心，因此 OpenClaw、TUI、Studio 共用同一套控制腦。當前 JSON 輸出包含 assistant 文本回復和 interaction session 資訊；真正的執行結果以工具結果和落盤檔案為準，不從模型口頭宣告推斷完成。 底層規劃、上下文組裝、寫作和審稿由同一 Harness action 排程，不再作為平行入口暴露。也可以在 ClawHub 搜尋 inkos 線上檢視。 Agent Skills InkOS 直接使用標準 SKILL.md 作為專業能力擴展，不再維護一套 InkOS 私有 Skill 協議。Skill 只向 Chat Agent 提供專業說明和靜態參考資料，不會增加執行許可權；建立、寫入、編輯和生成圖片仍然由 InkOS 工具與確認閘門控制。 可用方式： 放到標準目錄：專案 skills/ 、 .agents/skills/ ，或使用者目錄 ~/.agents/skills/ 、 ~/.openclaw/skills/ 。Studio 也可以匯入包含 SKILL.md 的完整資料夾和靜態參考資料；專案匯入統一儲存到 .agents/skills/ 。 或設定 INKOS_SKILL_DIRS=/abs/path/to/skills ，可指向單個 skill 目錄，也可指向包含多個 skill 子目錄的目錄。多個目錄按系統分隔符分隔。 在 Chat 裡用 @skill-id 強制本輪使用，例如： @detective-play 做一個證據鏈驅動的開放世界 。 不寫 @skill-id 時，Chat Agent 根據使用者當前意圖決定是否呼叫 use_skill ；不再通過 session 型別、關鍵詞或字串包含匹配機械啟用。 外部 Skill 只提供指令和靜態參考資料，InkOS 不會自動執行其中的指令碼；它也不會繞過現有工具許可權與確認閘門。 專業創作方法統一由 Skill 提供。要調整內建方法，可在 Studio 匯入同 ID 的專案 Skill 作為覆蓋；Agent 檔案只保留動態任務、上下文和工具協議。 最小 SKILL.md 示例： --- name : Detective Play description : Detective evidence and suspect-board play. --- Use evidence chains; do not turn clues into generic atmosphere. 配置 當前 InkOS 將 LLM 配置分成兩條清晰路徑： Studio 用視覺化服務配置 ， CLI / daemon / 部署環境支援 env 覆蓋 。兩者不會互相汙染。 方式一：Studio 服務配置（推薦） 適合本地寫作、Web 工作臺和視覺化管理。 inkos init my-novel cd my-novel
inkos 請從啟動日誌顯示的本機地址開啟 Studio。預設本地服務只接受同源瀏覽器請求；自定義嵌入或反向代理可通過服務啟動參數 allowedOrigins 明確配置可信來源。 開啟 Studio 後進入「模型配置」： 選擇服務商，例如 Google Gemini、Moonshot、MiniMax、智譜、百煉或自定義端點。 選擇協議型別：OpenAI Chat Completions、OpenAI Responses 或 Anthropic Messages；自定義端點應按上游實際協議選擇。 貼上 API Key，點選「測試連線」。 選擇可用模型，儲存配置。 回到書籍頁面開始寫作。 Studio 執行時只使用： provider bank 預設值
→ inkos.json 裡的 services / 當前 service / defaultModel
→ .inkos/secrets.json 裡的 service API Key 即使檢測到 ~/.inkos/.env 或專案 .env ，Studio 也只會展示提示，不會用 env 覆蓋 service、model、baseUrl 或 API Key。API Key 存在專案內的 .inkos/secrets.json ，不會寫進 inkos.json 。 方式二：CLI / daemon / 部署環境的 env 配置 適合終端批處理、伺服器部署、CI、Docker、守護程序和一次性切模型。 全域性 env： inkos config set-global \
  --provider < openai | anthropic | custom > \
  --base-url < API 地址 > \
  --api-key < 你的 API Key > \
  --model < 模型名 > 也可以手動寫 ~/.inkos/.env 或專案 .env ： INKOS_LLM_PROVIDER=custom
INKOS_LLM_BASE_URL=https://api.moonshot.cn/v1
INKOS_LLM_API_KEY=sk-...
INKOS_LLM_MODEL=kimi-k2.5 # 可選 INKOS_LLM_SERVICE=moonshot # 推薦寫；不寫時會盡量從 baseUrl 自動識別 INKOS_LLM_TEMPERATURE=0.7
INKOS_LLM_THINKING_BUDGET=0
INKOS_DEFAULT_LANGUAGE=zh
INKOS_LLM_EXTRA_top_p=0.9 CLI 合成順序： Studio/project service 配置
→ .inkos/secrets.json service key
→ global ~/.inkos/.env
→ project .env
→ 當前程序環境變數
→ CLI 參數 也就是說，CLI 預設可以複用 Studio 配好的服務和金鑰；如果 env 裡聲明瞭 INKOS_LLM_SERVICE 、 INKOS_LLM_MODEL 、 INKOS_LLM_BASE_URL 或 INKOS_LLM_API_KEY ，則作為覆蓋層生效。舊 env 只寫 baseUrl + model + apiKey 也能繼續用，InkOS 會盡量從 baseUrl 反推 service。 一次性指定服務或模型： inkos write next --service google --model gemini-2.5-flash
inkos write next --service moonshot --model kimi-k2.5 --no-stream
inkos agent " 繼續寫下一章 " --api-key-env MOONSHOT_API_KEY
inkos doctor --service minimaxCodingPlan --model MiniMax-M2.7 --service 會從 provider bank 自動推導 baseUrl、協議和相容策略； --model 必須屬於最終 service，否則會直接報錯，避免把 Kimi 模型發到 Gemini 這類錯配問題。 方式三：多模型路由（可選） 給不同 Agent 分配不同模型，按需平衡質量與成本： # 給不同 agent 配不同模型/提供商 inkos config set-model writer < model > --provider < provider > --base-url < url > --api-key-env < ENV_VAR > inkos config set-model auditor < model > --provider < provider > inkos config show-models # 檢視當前路由 未單獨配置的 Agent 自動使用全域性模型。 配置排查 inkos doctor doctor 會顯示當前 effective config mode、service/model/API Key 來源，並嘗試 API 連通性。常見模式： 模式 含義 studio-project Studio 執行時：只使用 Studio/project 配置和 secrets cli-project CLI 執行時：以 Studio 配置為基礎，再疊加 env 和 CLI 參數 environment CLI / daemon 直接使用當前環境配置 如果服務測試失敗，優先檢查服務商、模型和協議是否匹配。Google Gemini 的 AI Studio API Key 可用於 Gemini OpenAI-compatible endpoint；InkOS 會自動停用 Google 不支援的 OpenAI store 參數。MiniMax 預設走官方 OpenAI-compatible /v1/chat/completions ，並優先使用可工作的非流式 transport，避免流式返回 usage 但無正文的問題； MiniMax-M3* 會預設關閉 thinking 返回，M2.x thinking 由上游限制無法關閉。 LLM 配置更新 Studio / CLI 配置隔離 ：Studio 固定使用服務頁配置和 .inkos/secrets.json ；CLI、daemon、部署環境支援 env 覆蓋和一次性命令參數。 Provider bank 能力表 ：內建 Google Gemini、Moonshot、MiniMax、智譜、百鍊、DeepSeek、矽基流動、火山、騰訊混元、文心、訊飛星火、OpenRouter、kkaiapi、Ollama、CodingPlan 等服務的 baseUrl、協議、模型和相容策略。 模型歸屬校驗 ： --service google --model kimi-k2.5 這類錯配會直接報錯，避免把請求發到錯誤服務商。 Google Gemini 相容修復 ：AI Studio API Key 可直接用於 Gemini OpenAI-compatible endpoint，InkOS 會自動停用 Google 不支援的 OpenAI store 參數。

title: LodyAI/Lody
abstract:
Lody English | 簡體中文 A shared workspace for the coding agents your team already uses. Connect any machine and bring any coding agent through ACP. Share conversations with your team and dispatch work from desktop, mobile, web, or CLI. Documentation | Getting Started What you can do with Lody Share Agent conversations with your team Open the same conversation with your teammates. See the full transcript, runtime status, files, and code changes around the work, then add instructions without passing around screenshots or pasted logs. Bring the Agents and machines you already use Connect Claude Code, Codex, Kimi, OpenCode, or another ACP-compatible Agent. Keep using the subscriptions, logins, models, and permission modes configured on your laptops, workstations, servers, and cloud VMs. Machines remain private until their owner shares them with the workspace. Dispatch work from any surface Choose any connected machine when dispatching work from desktop, mobile, web, or CLI. Permission requests, progress, conversations, and code changes stay visible across these surfaces. Connect a machine Run Lody on a workstation, server, or cloud VM: npx lody daemon start The command opens a sign-in link, connects the machine to your workspace, and keeps it available for work dispatched from desktop, mobile, web, or CLI. Use Lody from the CLI The CLI is more than the process that connects a machine. From a terminal or script, you can register local projects; inspect workspaces, machines, linked repositories, and Agent configs; create and message sessions; read their history and status; or archive and restore them. Commands that support --json can also feed Lody workspace data into your own tools. npx lody session create --workspace my-team --agent-config codex \
  --repo owner/repo " Fix the failing test " npx lody session list --workspace my-team See the CLI documentation for the full command reference. Let Agents coordinate work across conversations Lody gives Agents tools to create or reuse other conversations, read their status and history, send follow-up instructions, cancel running work, and bring results back. This lets one conversation act as the coordinator: you can analyze a bug with a main Agent, then have it delegate investigation, implementation, and testing to separate conversations running in parallel. Lody keeps each child conversation independent while preserving its relationship to the conversation that created it. Conversations can also be referenced with an @ mention when you or an Agent needs to connect work across sessions. Keep code and execution in the same workspace Keep parallel work isolated Give sessions their own Git worktrees so Agents can work in parallel without mixing changes. Open multiple chats, files, diffs, terminals, and previews in tabs, or fork a session into another conversation or worktree to explore a different approach. Inspect changes where the work happened Browse project files and inspect per-turn or full-session diffs beside the conversation. Add line-level comments, follow pull request status and CI, and keep GitHub review threads close to the Agent that produced the change. Give Agents visual feedback Open a running web app inside the session, switch between responsive viewports, and send element-level visual annotations back to the Agent. More built in Agent Roles — share reusable Agent, model, permission, and instruction presets with the team. Attachments — send files and images from desktop, mobile, web, or CLI, and receive files produced by Agents. Session tools — search, pin, archive, fork, and organize conversations without losing their history. Desktop tools — use a built-in terminal, command palette, customizable shortcuts, and open files in your editor. Mobile controls — receive notifications, approve permission requests, inspect diffs, and follow active work with iOS Live Activities. Usage visibility — see context, token and quota usage, plus machine and Agent resource consumption. Beyond conversations Shared conversations are Lody's starting point, not the whole workspace. We plan to add documents and document sandboxes so teams can shape requirements, preserve decisions, and work with Agents outside the timeline of a single conversation. Over time, these tools can become shared team context for understanding not only what changed, but why. We want the entire workspace—not only conversations—to become local-first. Lody uses the Loro Stack, including Loro and Flock, to represent and synchronize collaborative state with CRDTs. The same foundation can extend from conversations to documents and future workspace tools. Our goal is for team context to become more durable and portable, and ultimately remain under the team's control. Lody is still moving toward full local-first support. Releases Pushing a stable vX.Y.Z tag creates a draft PR synchronizing every apps/*/package.json version on the default branch, followed by a GitHub Release
with generated changelog notes. No installers or auto-update files are built or
uploaded. The original tag is not moved; version synchronization takes effect
on the default branch after the PR is merged. GitHub Actions must be allowed to
create pull requests in repository settings. Bot-created PRs may require a maintainer
action to trigger CI. Existing releases and their assets are preserved on reruns. Repository apps/cli — Connect machines and run coding agents apps/electron — Lody desktop app apps/mobile — New native iOS and Android clients packages/components — Shared workspace UI packages/ui — Base UI primitives and StyleX design tokens packages/platform — Platform capabilities and integrations packages/shared — Shared schemas, protocols, and utilities packages/cloud-api — Optional-cloud protocol names and DTOs packages/e2ee-core — End-to-end encryption library: signed ledger, key delivery, services and adapters ( reading guide ). Product hosts: workspace bootstrap packages/e2ee-client — Personal-device E2EE host packages/e2ee-machine-sharing — Machine-service sharing policy packages/e2ee-lab — Local adversarial consumers and persistence probes for @lody/e2ee-core packages/turn-diff-store — Local content-addressed turn snapshots packages/loro-streams-rpc — RPC over Loro Streams packages/iroh-native — Native iroh transport for encrypted-workspace RPC ( rules ) packages/acp-extension-{core,kimi,pi} — ACP extension submodule workspaces. Kimi and Pi stay outside the root pnpm graph site-docs — Website, documentation, and blog See CONTRIBUTING.md for development setup and the community PR size policy. Mobile and upstream credit Lody’s new native mobile clients live in apps/mobile .
They are under active development and keep independent iOS and Android build
toolchains; see the mobile README for setup and current scope. The iOS client is built directly on Innei’s lody-ios .
We thank Innei and the upstream contributors for the
native app, chat experience, application architecture, and Loro/Flock protocol
runtime that made this work possible. Android also reuses a provenance-tracked
snapshot of that runtime. This is substantial foundational work, not merely
inspiration. Upstream licenses, notices, and additional acknowledgements are
preserved in the mobile credits .

title: martin-olivier/airgorah
abstract:
Airgorah A WiFi security auditing software Installation | Usage | Credits Airgorah is a WiFi security auditing software that can capture nearby WiFi traffic, discover clients connected to access points, perform deauthentication attacks, capture handshakes and PMKIDs, and crack the password of access points. It is written in Rust and uses GTK4 for the graphical part. ⭐ Don't forget to put a star if you like the project! Legal ⚠️ Airgorah is designed to be used in testing and discovering flaws in networks you are owner of. Performing attacks on WiFi networks you are not owner of is illegal in almost all countries. I am not responsible for whatever damage you may cause by using this software. Requirements This software only works on linux . The graphical interface runs as a normal
user (so it works under both X11 and Wayland ). When a privileged operation is
needed, it launches a small privileged agent ( airgorah-agent ) via polkit ,
which will prompt for authentication once. You will also need a wireless network card that supports monitor mode and packet injection . Installation The installation instructions are available here . Usage The documentation about the usage of the application is available here . License This project is released under MIT license. Contributing If you have any question about the usage of the application, do not hesitate to open a discussion If you want to report a bug or provide a feature, do not hesitate to open an issue or submit a pull request

title: aaif-goose/goose
abstract: goose your native open source AI agent — desktop app, CLI, and API — for code, workflows, and everything in between goose is a general-purpose AI agent that runs on your machine. Not just for code — use it for research, writing, automation, data analysis, or anything you need to get done. A native desktop app for macOS, Linux, and Windows. A full CLI for terminal workflows. An API to embed it anywhere. Built in Rust for performance and portability. goose works with 15+ providers — Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Ollama, OpenRouter, Azure, Bedrock, and more. Use API keys or your existing Claude, ChatGPT, or Gemini subscriptions via ACP . Connect to 70+ extensions via the Model Context Protocol open standard. goose is part of the Agentic AI Foundation (AAIF) at the Linux Foundation. Get started Download the desktop app for macOS, Linux, and Windows. Or install the CLI: curl -fsSL https://github.com/aaif-goose/goose/releases/download/stable/download_cli.sh | bash Quick links Quickstart Installation Tutorials Documentation Governance Custom Distributions — build your own goose distro with preconfigured providers, extensions, and branding Need help? Diagnostics & Reporting Known Issues a little goose humor 🪿 Why did the developer choose goose as their AI agent? Because it always helps them "migrate" their code to production! 🚀 goose around with us Discord YouTube LinkedIn Twitter/X

title: zeronsh/zeron
abstract:
Zeron Control your coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Devin, Grok, Hermes, Pi, Antigravity) locally by default, with optional multi-device sync. English | 簡體中文 | 한국어 | 日本語 | Español Desktop app Download the latest release for your platform from GitHub Releases : macOS — zeron-<version>-macos-arm64.dmg Windows — zeron-<version>-windows-x86_64-setup.exe Linux — zeron-<version>-linux-<arch>.tar.gz , then run its install.sh No account or network connection is needed; sessions stay on your device. The app updates itself. Headless (CLI) For servers and other machines without a display, such as a VPS that keeps agents running after you close your laptop. Linux only: curl -fsSL https://zeron.sh/install.sh | sh
zeron status The installer starts the engine as a background service that survives reboots. zeron status # local/synced mode and engine status zeron update # update to the latest release zeron daemon start | stop | restart | status Multi-device sync (optional) Sign in to start an agent on one device and follow or drive it from another: zeron daemon stop
zeron login # or: zeron logout to return to local-only zeron daemon start Devices signed in to the same account can read and write each other's workspace files, so only sign in devices you trust. Existing local sessions are never uploaded. Sponsors Thank you to The Context Company for sponsoring Zeron. You can help fund Zeron's development too by becoming a sponsor on GitHub . Developing or curious how it works? Ask DeepWiki or check out ARCHITECTURE.md . Licensed under the MIT License .

title: AI unlocks Gödel's notebooks, said to contain hundreds of proved theorems
abstract:
Gödel’s work inspired Alan Turing and paved the way for the digital age. Photograph: Alfred Eisenstaedt/The LIFE Picture Collection/Shutterstock View image in fullscreen Gödel’s work inspired Alan Turing and paved the way for the digital age. Photograph: Alfred Eisenstaedt/The LIFE Picture Collection/Shutterstock ‘Ahead of his time’: AI helps unlock discoveries hidden in notebooks of man who transformed maths Kurt Gödel left 1,009 pages of densely written text – much of it in an obsolete shorthand – which is now said to contain hundreds of proved theorems The Austrian logician Kurt Gödel was one of the most original thinkers of the 20th century. His two incompleteness theorems , published in 1931, transformed mathematics and paved the way for the digital age. After his seminal results of the 1930s, Gödel published only a few papers. His unpublished work, however, runs to tens of thousands of pages, and is of great interest to historians of science. Since 2017, the Finnish logician Jan von Plato has led a project at Helsinki University to understand the contents of 16 notebooks that Gödel wrote in the early 1940s. This material – the “workbooks” – is 1,009 pages of densely written text about maths and logic. Much of it is written in a German shorthand, Gabelsberger, that was obsolete even when Gödel was using it. Progress in the mathematical understanding of the text was painfully slow – about a page a week – until September, when von Plato enlisted the help of the AI model Claude. Within a couple of days, Claude had provided a comprehensive digest of the entire material, revealing Gödel had proved hundreds of theorems that no one knew about. The most famous logician of modern times had, in fact, discovered significantly more than anyone had thought. View image in fullscreen Albert Einstein presenting Kurt Gödel (second from right) with an award at Princeton University, where the two became friends. Photograph: Bettmann/Bettmann Archive “I was flabbergasted,” said von Plato. “The workbooks not only contain dozens of anticipations of results not known until the 70s and 80s, but they also contain 14 themes in logic that have not been pursued. Gödel was far ahead of his time.” Did you solve it? Gödel’s incompleteness theorem Read more Gödel changed the course of logic because he revealed the limits of mathematical knowledge. His incompleteness theorems show that in all mathematical systems there are true statements that can neither be proved or disproved. Yet while this result was a blow to previous generations of logicians, who had hoped that all truths were verifiable, Gödel’s work pushed the field in new directions, inspiring Alan Turing to write his 1936 paper that began the theory of modern computation. In 1940, Gödel fled Austria under the Nazis. He settled in Princeton, New Jersey, and became a close friend of Albert Einstein at the Institute of Advanced Study. Increasingly paranoid in his later years, he refused to eat food that was not cooked by his wife, and died of starvation in 1978. Von Plato said he had started his Gödel project in 2017 because he was facing mandatory retirement from Helsinki University. “What should I do to make myself indispensable? Oh yes, I’ll start reading Gödel’s enigmatic shorthand pages!” He received a €2.5m (£2.1m) grant from the European Research Council, taught himself Gabelsberger shorthand – “I am one of only six people who can read it in the world” – and assembled a small team. In August, at a conference in France about AI and theorem proving, von Plato met computer scientists who suggested that he co-opt the help of Claude in trying to make sense of the workbooks. On his return to Helsinki he began the process, showing Claude his transcriptions of the workbooks, as well as six books he had previously written on Gödel and other secondary scientific literature. “In a couple of days, I got to see a 650-page explanation of the workbooks. It had to be controlled page for page, but it’s basically a work that is impossible to do for human beings,” he said. “Humans read one page at a time and we tend to forget things. It takes us a year to read about 50 pages. We just are not able to keep in mind all the different parts. “The AI can connect all the pieces in a thousand pages. It can see all of Gödel’s writings as one piece.” skip past newsletter promotion after newsletter promotion View image in fullscreen A microfilm image of an example of Gödel’s shorthand from one of his notebooks. Photograph: Institute for Advanced Study Gödel’s incompleteness theorems revealed the existence of statements whose truths were independent of the system they were written in: that is, they could not be proved or disproved within the system. In 1966, the American mathematician Paul Cohen won the Fields medal, the highest honour in maths, for showing the independence of two well-known mathematical statements: the continuum hypothesis and the axiom of choice. Gödel reacted to Cohen’s Fields medal by saying that he had already proved the result in the 1940s. Yet when pushed for a proof by his peers, Gödel was unable to reconstruct one from his notes. The first task von Plato set Claude was to discover if Gödel’s workbooks had a proof of the independence of the axiom of choice, which would reveal that Gödel had been telling the truth in 1966. The answer came back: yes, almost. “He was just one step away,” said von Plato. “There’s one definition that Gödel got wrong, but he had the right definition two years earlier, and so the thought is that he would have arrived at the right definition anyway if he had just continued for a few months. For me, the architecture of his proof is just wonderful. It makes all of these results of set theory follow a uniform pattern. “What strikes me especially is that he starts from ideas. He’s not like someone who plays with formulas and hopes to arrive somewhere. He has very, very clear ideas, and then he’s methodical. Step after step he goes ahead and he manages to fulfil the aims that he has in this formal work.” Von Plato said that when Claude presented him with the reconstructed proof of the independence of the axiom of choice, he ran it through the proof assistant Coq, a program that verifies the validity of mathematical proofs, and it passed. Von Plato believes that had Gödel published his work on the axiom of choice, he would have won the 1940 Fields medal. “Maybe he felt that when Cohen got the medal, that that was something he sort of missed.” In further discussions with Claude, von Plato asked the AI model to extract all theorems in the workbooks for which Gödel either had a proof, had sketched a proof or had an idea for a proof. Claude found 663. When these results were put into Coq: “About 400 were verified as stated, about 200 were repaired, meaning that perhaps the statement of the theorem had to be made more precise, or some assumption had to be added. About 50 were false, and this is no wonder. Gödel himself, when rereading his notes, would occasionally add a marginal remark: falsch! [incorrect] or schlecht! [bad].” Von Plato added: “I am sure that the continued study of Gödel’s manuscripts will reveal further treasures. The workbooks contain, Claude says, more than a dozen themes in logic and foundations of mathematics that have not been found in the 80-plus years since they were written down. So this is one thing to explore. But there are many others. His physics and cosmology notebooks are an unknown territory I plan to start exploring once I am finished with my present logic projects.” Joel David Hamkins, a professor of logic at the University of Notre Dame, Indiana, has not seen Claude’s reconstruction of Gödel’s proof of the independence of the axiom of choice, but said that if it stood up “it is remarkable and historically interesting. Although how much is Claude and how much is Gödel is a job for the historians.

title: No AI Slop: A Manifesto
abstract:
No AI Slop: A Manifesto Written by the speakers and attendees of AIE Code Summit 2026 In 2001, 17 software engineers and leaders got together at a ski lodge in Snowbird, Utah to understand the biggest challenge of their time: heavyweight, documentation-driven software development processes. Out of this we got the Agile Manifesto , four values and twelve principles that changed how most of the industry builds software. Today we convene to build our own manifesto - the No AI Slop manifesto. AI increasingly helps us write our code, docs, plans, and messages. We've all been on the receiving end of slop, and most of us have sent some too. Through this work, we have come to value: Outcomes over output Understanding over speed Our own thinking over a model's first draft Better work over easier work Improving the system over patching the output The world moves especially fast these days, but the goal of these resolutions is to embrace our important human role in harnessing AI safely, responsibly, in a way that creates value for everyone, and that will be relevant for years to come. We believe: AI is the most useful tool most of us have ever worked with, but a swarm of agents can produce more work in a single day than a person can review in our lifetime. Slop is when we put less effort into producing something than we ask the consumer to spend understanding it. Using AI doesn't necessarily make something slop. Slop happens when we pass AI output along without taking responsibility for the quality or the reader's experience. AI cannot replace human judgement, it can only amplify our judgement (or lack thereof). Slop is asymmetric. The cost of producing a thousand-line PR or a ten-page doc is approaching zero, while the cost of reviewing it remains constant. In code, even before AI, slop proliferates when we repeatedly work around problems instead of solving them correctly. It comes from tools that lean HEAVILY toward adding rather than subtracting. A lot of slop comes from pressure. Companies are pushing their people to redefine what is humanly possible. Slop compounds. The more slop sits in our knowledge base, in chat, in code, the more of it the next agent reads and copies. The more slop flying around a team, the more we lose the will to fight it. Communication and quality get worse over time, not better. Thus we the undersigned resolve that: Human time and attention is incredibly valuable, so we optimize for using it wisely. We fight slop because AI should make our work better, not just easier. We optimize systems, tools, and products for efficient elicitation of human intent and for efficient human understanding. We do our own thinking when working with a model. We explore resources, code, and prior art to truly understand the problem before the work starts. We own the intent, taste, and consequences of what we ship, however much AI helps us make it. When an agent wrote something we're sending, we make that clear, and we check the parts that matter before it goes out. When someone sends us slop, we tell them, kindly, and ask them to review it first. Most of us have needed that same note at some point. There will always be alpha in reviewing something . As models improve, we may stop reading most of the code. We may still review a plan, design, or result, because if we don't, we just get the same output as everyone else. Agent reviews, linters, and verifiers are useful but not sufficient. For now, we still review at least some subset of the outputs. What subset depends on the stakes. What shipped, who's using it, and how it's helping them matters FAR MORE than lines of code, prs merged, tokens spent, or the number of agents running in parallel. Unreviewed output isn't always necessarily bad. One-shot prompts and vibe coding are high leverage tools. "Slop" is bad when it undermines our outcome -- a useful product, a maintainable system, or saving ourselves and our teammates time and energy. When a mistake shows up twice, we scale ourselves and our team by improving the system and its guardrails. Anything a linter, type checker, or automated check can catch, we let it catch. And finally: None of us has this figured out. We're each relearning what we will and won't accept, and there's no single right answer. Again, the world moves especially fast these days, but the goal of these resolutions is to embrace our important human role in harnessing AI safely, responsibly, in a way that creates value for everyone, and that will be relevant for years to come. We look forward to working with the community to evolve these beliefs as the world changes. Comments and feedback on this document are welcome. What is slop? Why does slop happen? Why is slop worth fighting? How do we fight slop? Special thanks to Philip Kiely, Swyx, Lucas Meijer, Rebecca Bakels, Tejas Kumar, Natalie Serrino, Francisco Javier Arceo, Kent C. Dodds, Ankit Jain, Brandon Waselnuk, Mihail Eric, Justin McCarthy, Raz Berman Gold, Yacine Mahdid, Justin Poehnelt, Lauren Tan, and Kyle Mistele for contributions to this project. title: Anthropic upgrades Claude Code Projects to run parallel AI workers
abstract:
Managing multiple sessions across a build used to require you to divide the work, juggle handoffs, and stitch the results back together. Now in a Claude Code project, you describe what needs to get done and Claude manages the work. Claude scopes the request, delegates the work, coordinates parallel threads, reviews the outputs, and assembles the finished result. You can steer progress throughout, even from your phone, and it keeps working after you step away from your computer. For example, configure a project and set a goal to reduce your app's checkout p75 latency. Then ask Claude to profile each endpoint, test optimizations, and open PRs in parallel threads. Or connect your API, web, and mobile repos and set a goal to retire a deprecated v1 endpoint. Claude creates a thread per repo to migrate the callers, run the tests, open PRs, and then tells you which ones need to merge first. Starting today, updated projects are available in beta to select Claude Pro and Max subscribers who use cloud sessions in Claude Code and don’t have any existing projects on the web or desktop. Over the coming week, we'll expand access to more Claude Code users on those plans. Updated projects across all of Claude and Team and Enterprise plans come after that. If you're on Pro or Max and don't have access yet, you can join the waitlist . Existing projects on Pro and Max plans keep working as they do today. We'll upgrade them as the rollout expands to chat and Cowork. Threads do the work, Claude directs it Projects have threads that do the work and a coordinator that directs them. When you start a project, you select a goal as well as the repo or context. Claude starts by suggesting work it can pick up right away. You can configure the project’s cloud environment, connectors, plugins, instructions, and model. You can monitor and guide progress in the main project chat, or dive into each individual thread to examine and steer the details. Brief Claude in the project the way you'd brief a chief of staff and it routes work to new or pre-existing threads. Claude also checks in and follows through on work. With repositories connected, a thread opens pull requests and runs your tests; with documents, it reads them and drafts. Under the hood, each thread is a Claude Code cloud session working on its own branch and copy of the repo. The coordinator keeps work organized, but if any threads work on the same code, the overlap is resolved as a merge conflict just like any other PR. Each thread can further split its delegated work into pieces using subagents, loops, and workflows when needed so large assignments finish faster. Context builds over time Projects are designed for long-running or agentic workflows: work that takes longer than one reply and has more than one part. Over time, Claude learns more about the project details and applies them to its work. Every thread now adds to and draws from a shared memory, reducing the need for complex prompt engineering. For example, Claude can remember the release moved to Friday, why the export was dropped, or who to check in with before touching the billing service. One project across a week. Each request opens a thread on the right; the memory, the decisions, and the results build underneath. Claude also remembers your working and communication style. You can ask it to adjust how often it checks in, how frequently it starts new threads, or how detailed to make each update. Alongside memory, projects now include a library that collects the files you add and the artifacts produced by Claude. This makes it easier to find relevant materials and for new work to build on past efforts. What's next Projects can run several threads at once, and each one is a full Claude Code session. Because of this, projects can reach usage limits faster. You can check project specific usage and select the model and effort levels used by the coordinator chat as well as the worker threads. Threads run in the cloud today; running on your machine alongside your local tools and code and behind your network is coming very soon. Start using projects .

title: Show HN: A terminal-native idle factory game, written in Rust with ratatui
abstract:
Hey HN readers! I'm snipedbywifi ( https://gitlab.com/snipedbywifi ), and i've been working on terminactory. Please try it out if you'd like to play a cozy factory game while waiting for long agent tasks to finish! The game is a factory game (overused niche, i know xD), but runs in your terminal. Reason i built it? glad you asked: So basically, it started off with me wanting a terminal-native factory game. Me and the modern 5.5 claude models made a base for the game that I liked, and then i went ham adding features / fixing some minor flaws (like adding claude code hooks so you recieve "telegrams" [the agent's responses], so you can review progress directly in-game). (yes, I had heavy AI assistance, disclaimer!!!) Right now, the game has basic factory features you'd expect from a game like this (build stuff, delete stuff, measure how much you're earning, basic selection tools), along with a few more.. "unexpected" features. This includes a fake in-game browser that has a wiki, fake forums, some fun bits of lore, some more lore, a LOT more lore, and a research graph that shows how many items or how much RP (research points) you'd need to unlock something, and some more QOL features. If anyone actually has this issue / want of a terminal-based game that runs alongside your agents so you don't doomscroll, do you have any suggestions, or additional ideas I could add? It's hosted on GitLab, soo, that's one additional thing i'd like to mention Thanks for reading!! snipedbywifi (p.s. first HN post lol)

title: How Not to Build a Music Player
abstract:
How Not to Build a Music Player November 13, 2026 The Twelve-Day War made me realize online music players aren’t a viable option for those who live under an oppressive regime that disconnects the internet across the country as a way to silence public opinion. So, as soon as the connection came back, I started archiving tracks and looking for offline alternatives and discovered Strawberry . It’s a feature-rich music player and kept me happy for quite a while, but I have this habit of looking at song lyrics and singing along! Strawberry fetches lyrics from the internet when it recognizes a song, but sometimes the lyrics weren’t line-synced and worse, it displayed the timestamps next to the lyrics which I found pretty annoying to look at. I wasn’t aware of other music players such as foobar2000 which my friend just pointed me to while writing this post. I decided to write my own music player and call it AMP with a few goals in mind: minimal feature-set, no C++ dependencies, proper system integration to make it feel like a native app, and of course, write it in Zig (including the shaders!). I also wanted to roll my own UI because of the fun memories of working on V’s UI during my first days of being introduced into system programming. But before I could make any meaningful progress, a new wave of protests started. Following the tragedy of January 8 and 9 , another internet blackout began, lasting more than four months. During the blackout, there were these anonymous people on Telegram selling internet access through personal White SIMs , whitelisted servers, Starlink dishes, etc. A black market had formed for the freaking internet! You’d get charged $5 or more for just 1GB of traffic. The prices dropped slightly after a while, but it was still hella expensive. The regime surely made a lot of money out of it. I ended up spending hundreds of dollars on these services and other methods just to stay in touch with my friends and keep my hobbies alive. Killing time was becoming a problem. Especially for someone like me who built their entire social life online. I carefully used this slow connection to download repositories, documention, etc. to continue working on my music player. It really brought me immense joy during this hard time. Screenshot from 2026/5/25 Once the connection was mostly restored to the pre-blackout days (UDP traffic is still blocked, though, which naturally also affects QUIC), my attention was shifted towards LLMs. It had become very hard for me to ignore the hype and progress around frontier LLMs. As I really never thought about using them seriously for coding. They are still everywhere in the news, and I was just reminded that I owned a Claude Max 20x subscription gift from my boss back in 2025. Eating dust and maybe soon expiring. So I decided to give it a try and experiment on my music player. It was a very addictive experience. I literally couldn’t hit the plan limits no matter how hard I tried, so after a few non-stop days of prompting, a good chunk of AMP was vibecoded.. At the time, I thought this was an okay approach for a hobby project and I could just un-slopify it later. Little did I know I’m mentally incapable of reviewing tens of thousands lines of code. Shortly after, Anthropic figured that I live in Iran and instantly banned my account. Then Codeberg announced its no-AI policy , which gave me two choices. Either get rid of all that slop or move the repository elsewhere. Going with the former option, I started reading every single line of code, rewriting them. I was surprised by my own ignorance and how much LLMs like to complicate stuff. (I wish I could show an example, but my memory is extremely fragile and I’ve got no pre-rewrite history of the repo to check). Four months later, nearly half the codebase is gone, and somehow it’s more robust with the same set of features (and more). I regret relying on LLMs in the first place, but hey, lesson learned. That said I think it’s still possible to create a healthy relationship with LLMs as long as you look at them as a fancy IDE feature. A lot of times they are just running long sed or regex commands that are a no-brainer act for humans when done by hand but still consumes a good time. For now and hopefully forever I think I’ll be going the old school way. Never rush your hobbies! Btw this is how AMP looks like right now! v0.1 Worth mentioning that the blur shader is written in Zig based on this excellent blog post! . Roadmap to v1.0: Music server Android and Windows support Packaging for major Linux distros Any suggestions? ← Zig and GPUs

title: Live-migration support in FreeBSD and bhyve coming
abstract:
This project presents a first working state for live migration of bhyve guests on FreeBSD 15.1. A running amd64 guest can move between two hosts over TCP while continuing to run; it is paused only for the final stop-and-copy phase. The work builds on bhyve's experimental snapshot support and adds dirty-page tracking in the vmm kernel module together with a migration protocol in bhyve and bhyvectl. Live migration of a VM in FreeBSD with bhyve I previously discussed the state of bhyve live migration, its historical development, existing limitations, and why it matters for the future of FreeBSD virtualization in my article bhyve on FreeBSD and VM Live Migration – Quo vadis? . The goal is deliberately practical: make it possible to test, discuss, and improve a real implementation rather than discuss live migration only in the abstract. The current code and test tooling are being published as a WIP RFC so that the next steps can be shaped in the open. A more detailed demonstration of a VM being live migrated can be watched on my YouTube channel . Why this matters Live migration is an important building block for enterprise virtualisation. It enables host maintenance, hardware replacement, load balancing, and failure-domain management with far less disruption to workloads. It is also central to the Sylve project, which aims to offer a Proxmox-like virtualisation solution for FreeBSD. Migration is not an optional convenience in that kind of platform; it is one of the capabilities that makes clustered operations practical. It is equally important for BoxyBSD, where I offer free BSD-based VPS instances to individuals. Without a credible migration path, routine host work can require a guest outage. That makes live migration a current show stopper for the project, and is why this work is being pushed toward a testable, reviewable state. How the current implementation works The source starts with a pre-copy phase. It sends populated guest memory, then repeatedly obtains a bitmap of pages changed since the previous scan and sends only those pages. Once the remaining dirty set fits the configured downtime target, stops shrinking, or reaches the configured round limit, bhyve pauses the guest and its devices. It then sends the final dirty pages and the existing snapshot state for the vCPUs, kernel state, and emulated devices. The destination validates the basic VM geometry, receives memory and state, restores it, and reports that it is ready. Only then does the source send GO , the commit point. Before GO , a failed migration can resume the source guest. The destination does not start the guest if it does not receive that commit message. A warm, stop-and-copy mode is available too, which is useful both as a fallback and as a comparison baseline. What is implemented today Pre-copy and warm migration: live pre-copy is configurable with downtime and maximum-round controls; explicit stop-and-copy migration is also supported. Multi-vCPU protocol support: the migration handshake carries the guest vCPU count, the destination refuses a count mismatch, and all guest vCPUs are paused and resumed as part of migration. The published test bed has primarily exercised a one-vCPU guest, so multi-vCPU stress and race testing remain required before making broader claims. Memory consistency checks: dirty-page tracking covers guest and mapped emulation writes through page dirty state, while vmm write holds are recorded separately. The test workload rewrites and verifies guest memory and reports any missing or stale page as a mismatch. Repeated ping-pong migrations have been used to check that the workload continues without errors. Disk-write validation: a guest-side workload repeatedly writes and fsyncs files, verifies checksums, and is checked again after a cold reboot. This is intended to exercise the device pause, drain, and restore path. Failure handling: destination refusal, an unreachable target, and a target disappearing during both pre-copy and stop-and-copy have been tested. Before commit, the source is intended to resume the paused guest after failure. Basic destination checks: protocol version, page size, memory layout, and vCPU count are checked before data transfer. The migration socket is opened by bhyvectl and passed into bhyve so that bhyve can remain inside its Capsicum sandbox. Supported scope: this is amd64-only and depends on the experimental BHYVE_SNAPSHOT support. It relies on snapshot-capable emulated devices; PCI passthrough is not migratablem, yet. Observed results In the current two-host test environment, repeated live migrations, memory-rewrite workloads, and fsync-heavy disk workloads have completed successfully. For a slowly dirtying 512 MiB guest, observed downtime has been roughly 138–171 ms. A rapidly dirtying guest may not converge during pre-copy, but still falls back to a correct stop-and-copy completion with a longer pause. These are encouraging engineering results, not a production support promise or a complete correctness proof. Blockers before upstreaming can be evaluated further The following are neutral engineering requirements, not criticism of the value of the prototype. They need to be addressed first before further upstreaming into FreeBSD can be evaluated responsibly. Prove and harden dirty-log correctness. The kernel-side dirty-page algorithm must be demonstrated not to lose a write while dirty bits are examined and cleared. It needs focused concurrency, paging, emulation-write, and multi-vCPU stress coverage, plus a reviewable locking and memory-ordering argument. Define a complete compatibility contract. Matching memory size and vCPU count is not enough. A destination should verify guest identity, CPU capabilities, bhyve/vmm and snapshot format compatibility, device topology and capabilities, and shared-storage identity before accepting a migration. Harden the transport and protocol. The current TCP transport has no authentication or encryption and uses a first-version native protocol. A stable protocol needs explicit wire formats, bounded message handling, timeouts, version negotiation, authentication or a supported external secure transport model, and clear operational guidance. Clarify the commit and device-side-effect boundary. The source/destination handoff must be reviewed so that device restoration cannot cause externally visible work before the source has committed, and so that the unavoidable uncertain outcome after a lost post-commit acknowledgement is operationally recoverable. Specify storage and network handoff. Shared storage must have defined coherency, durability, and fencing assumptions. Network migration also needs a clear answer for tap/bridge handling, MAC/IP movement, and traffic convergence. Build an in-tree test strategy. The current scripts and test-bed workloads are useful, but upstream review will need automated regression coverage and a documented support matrix across CPU counts, memory sizes, supported devices, host CPUs, and failure cases. Separate the work into reviewable patches. Dirty-page tracking, snapshot API refactoring, protocol/receiver work, CLI changes, and tests should be independently reviewable. This will make design feedback more actionable and reduce the risk of merging coupled changes. Next steps We have already had deeper discussions about these questions in the Sylve Discord. Publishing this current state is intended to make those discussions more concrete, bring in wider FreeBSD and bhyve feedback, and turn the prototype into a clear roadmap. The immediate focus is correctness, compatibility validation, transport safety, and repeatable tests—not adding performance features first. Currently, some peopel already have access to it and it's planned ot publish this at least as a proposal on my git and GitHub at: git.gyptazy.com/gyptazy/freebsd-bhyve-live-migration github.

title: Show HN: DeepSeek V3 in ~200 lines of pure Jax
abstract:
DeepSeek V3 in pure JAX The architecture from the DeepSeek-V3 technical report in 190 lines of pure JAX , pretrained from scratch on a MacBook Air on public-domain detective fiction. No Flax, no Equinox, no PyTorch. Params are plain dicts of arrays and every part of the model is a function you can read top to bottom in deepseek_v3.py . Read the write-up: DeepSeek V3 in 190 lines of pure JAX , with diagrams, the code explained piece by piece, and the results. What's in the 190 lines Idea from the paper What it does Where Multi-head Latent Attention (MLA) Caches one small latent per token instead of full keys and values: 480 → 144 numbers per token per layer here mla , init_cache Decoupled RoPE One rotary key shared by all heads, kept outside the compressed latent rope , apply_rope , mla DeepSeekMoE 1 shared expert that always runs + 16 routed experts, top-4 per token route , moe Auxiliary-loss-free balancing A per-expert bias nudges routing toward idle experts; it changes which experts are picked, not their weights update_bias , route Sequence-wise balance loss The small complementary loss from the paper (α = 1e-4) seq_balance_loss Multi-token prediction (MTP) An extra module also predicts the token after next, weighted λ = 0.3 in the loss forward , loss_fn Training and generation bf16 compute on f32 master weights; prefill + decode with the MLA cache make_train_step , generate Results One run of the default config on a MacBook Air M5 (24 GB): Model 36.2M parameters, 13.6M active per token Data 207 books, 21.7M training tokens (Hammett repeated 3×); validation is held-out crime fiction Training 12,000 steps, ~98M tokens (~4.5 epochs), ~2.6 h Speed ~10.7k tokens/s (median) Validation loss 5.02 (step 250) → 3.51 Expert load, with bias 5.7–6.9% per expert (even is 6.25%), at step 2000 Expert load, without bias 0.09–18.6% per expert, at step 2000 With balancing on and off, validation loss at step 2000 was the same (3.921 vs 3.923). The bias evens out the experts without costing anything, which is the paper's claim. Its own words, from the prompt "The fog came in off the": The fog came in off the bay, and the great trees were spreading and the stars were shining. This is an architecture demo, not a strong language model. See the write-up for what worked, what didn't, and what's missing. Try the trained model The v1.0 release has the exact checkpoint and data from the published run. After installing (step 1): mkdir -p data runs/main
curl -L -o runs/main/ckpt.pkl https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/deepseek-v3-jax/releases/download/v1.0/ckpt.pkl # 138 MB curl -L -o data/tokenizer.json https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/deepseek-v3-jax/releases/download/v1.0/tokenizer.json
.venv/bin/python sample.py --prompt " The fog came in off the " --num 3 The checkpoint is a Python pickle, which can run code when loaded. Only load checkpoints from sources you trust. Reproduce it You need an Apple Silicon Mac, Python 3.12 and uv . The published run used 24 GB of memory. No Mac? See Running on CPU . 1. Install git clone https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/deepseek-v3-jax.git && cd deepseek-v3-jax
uv venv -p 3.12 .venv
uv pip install --python .venv/bin/python -r requirements.txt Every version in requirements.txt is pinned. jax-metal 0.1.1 only works with jax==0.4.34 , so don't upgrade JAX. 2. Check your setup JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu .venv/bin/pytest tests.py -q # 39 passed .venv/bin/python smoke_metal.py # optional: what jax-metal supports on your Mac In smoke_metal.py , "grad through 2-axis contraction" fails on jax-metal 0.1.1. That's expected, and the model is written to avoid it. 3. Build the dataset .venv/bin/python prepare_data.py This downloads the 207 books in sources.txt (~120 MB, about 7 minutes), cleans them, trains an 8,192-token BPE tokenizer and writes data/train.bin , data/val.bin and data/tokenizer.json . It should print: train: 211 docs, 83.4M chars, 21.69M tokens
val: 4 docs, 1.1M chars, 0.30M tokens The published run's data had these hashes: shasum -a 256 data/train.bin data/val.bin data/tokenizer.json d37aca97e707bb81b6e4d266cc1adfd1f3e3556457c6eb724e495118a734e0bb data/train.bin
b7ac285b115e6793b5d36aa5b4bc6e81a5fccfc7af0908a306d3828ebca9c31c data/val.bin
c5a142b4006a967c880dda44ad792719d53c16d947da3b6c2332d6132d9967cc data/tokenizer.json You will most likely get different hashes. The Hammett books are pinned to exact Standard Ebooks commits and come out identical, but Project Gutenberg files can't be pinned, and Gutenberg has since re-issued 28 of the 203 books with small edits (mostly accents stripped, like "José" → "Jose"). The token counts come out the same, so training should behave the same. To train on the exact same bytes , skip prepare_data.py and download the published data instead: mkdir -p data for f in train.bin val.bin tokenizer.json ; do curl -L -o data/ $f https://github.com/Vaibhaav-Tiwari/deepseek-v3-jax/releases/download/v1.0/ $f ; done shasum -a 256 data/ * .bin data/tokenizer.json # should match the hashes above 4. Train .venv/bin/python train.py # the main run: 12k steps, ~2.6 h .venv/bin/python train.py --steps 2000 --out runs/bias_on # balancing ablation, with the bias .venv/bin/python train.py --steps 2000 --out runs/bias_off --no-bias # ...and without it Each run writes metrics.jsonl (loss, validation loss, per-expert load, biases, tokens/s) and ckpt.pkl (saved at every evaluation) into its --out folder, which defaults to runs/main . Seeds are fixed, but GPU math on Metal isn't bit-for-bit deterministic, so expect your numbers to land close to the ones above rather than match them exactly. 5. Generate .venv/bin/python sample.py --prompt " The fog came in off the " --num 3 Defaults: temperature 0.8, top-k 50, 300 new tokens per sample ( --temp , --top-k , --n ). 6. Make the figures .venv/bin/python plots.py # needs runs/main, runs/bias_on, runs/bias_off JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu .venv/bin/python charts.py # the rest of the write-up's charts Both write into post/figures/ . To redraw the figures without training, download the logs from the release: metrics-main.jsonl , metrics-bias_on.jsonl and metrics-bias_off.jsonl go into runs/main/ , runs/bias_on/ and runs/bias_off/ as metrics.jsonl . charts.py also needs the checkpoint and the data. Running on CPU Everything runs without jax-metal. It's much slower, so use the smaller config: JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu .venv/bin/python train.py --config small --config small (4 layers, 8 experts, top-2, 128-token context) is meant for 8–16 GB Macs too. It has only been checked for a couple of steps, not trained to the end. Files File What it is deepseek_v3.py The model : config, MLA, MoE, balancing, MTP, loss, train step, cached generation. The 190 lines. train.py Training loop: AdamW with warmup and cosine decay, evaluation, checkpoints, logging prepare_data.py , sources.txt Download, clean and tokenize the corpus sample.py Text generation from a checkpoint tests.py 39 tests: causal masking, cache vs full forward, routing, balancing, MTP targets, NaN handling, bf16 master weights, and more smoke_metal.py Which JAX operations work on Apple's GPU plots.py , charts.py The figures, all drawn from the logs, checkpoint and corpus post/ Diagrams, figures and screenshots from the write-up "190 lines" counts the non-blank, non-comment lines of deepseek_v3.py after its docstring: tail -n +5 deepseek_v3.py | grep -cvE ' ^\s*(#|$) ' # 190 What's simplified Dense MoE compute. Every expert runs on every token and the unpicked ones are zeroed. The routing math is exact, but there's no sparse dispatch or expert parallelism. No weight absorption in MLA. The latent is decompressed explicitly, which is easier to read and slower at inference. Not included: FP8 training, DualPipe, node-limited routing, YaRN context extension, and any post-training. Scale. 36.2M parameters vs 671B, 6 layers vs 61, a 256-token context vs 128K.

title: Show HN: Agweb – a browser for agents that stays out of your way
abstract:
agweb A browser for coding agents on macOS, built on WebKit (Safari's engine). I run several coding agents at once, and Playwright's Chrome windows kept stealing my keyboard, while headless browsers got blocked by some sites and left me guessing what went wrong. agweb is one window that never takes focus: agents drive it from the shell with agweb , a playwright-cli-style command, and you watch them all live. Idle tabs are suspended: on my Mac five open pages sit at 0% CPU, where Chrome's GPU process kept five to seven cores busy. Five idle pages Memory agweb 590 MB Headless Chrome 730 MB Playwright Chrome 1.6 GB Never steals focus. No window comes to the front, nothing pops up. Dialogs, changing tabs, file pickers and downloads are answered in code. You can always see it. The dashboard (⌘D) shows every tab of every agent at once, live, with each agent's last command. And it is always a real window: some sites block headless browsers, and headless leaves you guessing what went wrong. Many agents at once. Each agent works in its own workspace with its own tabs, grouped by agent in the sidebar. Log in once. A named profile ( -p work ) keeps its logins and is shared by every agent using it, at the same time. Light. Idle tabs are throttled and then suspended, so open pages cost almost nothing once nobody uses them. Acts like a person. Clicks and keys are native macOS events, and the pointer moves like a hand, so hover menus and drag-and-drop work. Made for agents. Snapshots give each element a ref that lasts while it is on the page. snapshot --diff and find show only what matters, and every action reports what it changed. Passwords stay out of the transcript. fill --secret-cmd 'pass show site' types a secret the agent never sees in replies. 1Password and Bitwarden CLIs work too. No ads. Ads and trackers are blocked with uBlock Origin's lists, which agweb downloads every 4 days. An agent testing analytics can turn it off for its own workspace ( agweb -w task adblock off ). Demo videos. video-start records a tab to MP4, with the pointer and clicks drawn in. Install Needs macOS 26 or later. Download Agweb.dmg from Releases , drag Agweb to Applications and open it. Then: Help ▸ Install Command Line Tool Help ▸ Install Agent Skill (for Claude Code and Codex). Both are links into the app, so they update with it. To build from source instead (Xcode 26 or later): ./scripts/build.sh
build/Agweb.app/Contents/Helpers/agweb install-cli
agweb install-skill Use agweb -w task open en.wikipedia.org/wiki/WebKit # a workspace for this task; starts the app if needed agweb -w task snapshot # the page as a tree with [ref=eN] handles agweb -w task click ' role=button[name="Main menu"] ' The click's reply already says what it did, so the agent needs no second snapshot: ### Changes - navigation "Site" [ref=e2]
- - button "Main menu" [ref=e3]
+ - button "Main menu" [checked] [expanded] [ref=e3]
+ - list [ref=e1167]
+ - listitem [ref=e1168]
+ - link "Main page" [ref=e1169] agweb help lists every command. Settings (⌘,) has text size, dashboard columns, a CPU and memory readout and the ad blocker switch. Compared with playwright-cli Same commands where possible, so agents already know them; a Playwright name it lacks suggests its own ( scroll-to → scroll-into-view ). On top: Replies say what changed : fetches started, lines added or removed, dialogs, popups, downloads, console errors. No snapshot after every step, so far fewer tokens. Refs last while the element is on the page. ask hands the tab to you for a login, MFA code or CAPTCHA, without taking focus. Actions wait for the fetches they caused, so agents rarely sleep. text returns the page's article as markdown. Shared logins : agents on one profile run at once; a Chrome profile opens in one browser only. Limits WebKit only: no Chrome DevTools Protocol, so Playwright and Chrome extensions can't attach, and Chrome-only sites may misbehave. route mocks fetch and XHR only; requests lists images, scripts and styles by URL only ( --static ). The ad blocker can't run uBlock's scripts, so YouTube ads and some "turn off your ad blocker" walls get through. For what it can't do, use Playwright. Develop ./scripts/selftest.sh runs every command against a local page in a separate instance; swift test runs the unit tests. AGWEB_ROOT=/tmp/dir starts a second instance beside your own that keeps everything in that folder. Defuddle (MIT) is bundled for text .
